summary: Procedural framework for ultrasound-guided peripheral nerve blocks. LA max dosing and the LAST/lipid-rescue protocol are the single source of truth in their own modules — cross-linked, not restated.

body.text: Ten safety rules: (1) IV access before the needle goes in — always. (2) 20% lipid emulsion physically at the bedside before the first mL. (3) Calculate the total mg dose, not just volume. (4) A negative aspiration does NOT exclude intravascular placement (false-negative up to 2%). (5) Inject 2-3 mL aliquots, aspirate between each. (6) Never inject without a confirmed needle-tip position. (7) High injection resistance → stop and reposition. (8) Nerve swelling on US during injection → STOP (intraneural). (9) Paresthesia on injection → stop and reposition. (10) Monitor 30 minutes post-injection — LAST can be delayed.
Local anesthetic selection (calculate the mg dose)

items: Dexamethasone 4-8 mg perineural extends the block ~4-8 h (an equivalent IV dose may do the same).

Epinephrine 1:200,000 (5 mcg/mL) prolongs the block, cuts vascular uptake, and acts as an intravascular marker — a test-dose HR rise > 20 bpm within 60 s suggests IV injection (unreliable with β-blockade or baseline tachycardia).
Dexmedetomidine 0.5-1 mcg/kg perineural — emerging duration extension, not universally adopted.

1. PRE-PROCEDURE — indication + consent (LAST, nerve injury, hematoma, infection, block failure; + pneumothorax for interscalene/supraclavicular, phrenic palsy for C3-C5). Absolute CI: refusal, infection over the site, LA-class allergy. Relative: coagulopathy/anticoagulation (use ASRA thresholds — see neuraxial-anticoagulation), pre-existing neuropathy in the distribution, contralateral phrenic palsy. Document baseline motor/sensory. IV access confirmed. Lipid emulsion + airway kit + reduced-dose epi at the bedside.

2. US SETUP — high-frequency linear (< 4 cm targets), low-frequency curvilinear (> 4-5 cm). Systematic survey scan with colour Doppler (never skip). Confirm nerve identity by tracing proximally/distally — honeycomb fascicular pattern in short axis. Optimise depth/gain/focus/anisotropy tilt before the needle.

3. STERILE TECHNIQUE — chlorhexidine (fully dry), sterile probe cover with gel inside, sterile drape. Continuous catheter → maximal barrier. Skin wheal 0.5-1 mL 1% lidocaine. 21-22 G echogenic needle; length = target depth + approach angle.

4. NEEDLE INSERTION — in-plane preferred (whole shaft + tip visible). Never advance if the tip is not visible. Confirm tip with hydrodissection (0.5-2 mL D5W — better echogenicity, non-neurotoxic); fluid should open the correct plane and separate nerve from fascia.

5. INJECTION — aspirate 3-5 s before every aliquot. Inject 2-3 mL aliquots, pause 15-30 s each, total ≥ 60-90 s. Target pressure < 15 psi. STOP for paresthesia, high resistance, or nerve swelling on US. Correct spread = hypoechoic 'donut' around the nerve in short axis. Reposition for partial spread rather than adding volume.

6. POST-PROCEDURE — monitor SpO₂/ECG/NIBP ≥ 30 min. Assess block onset (cold, pinprick, light touch, motor) at 5-min intervals vs baseline; onset 10-25 min for long-acting agents. Document agent/conc/volume/total mg, adjuvants, aspiration results, US spread, onset checks, symptoms. Limb protection + fall precautions (any lower-extremity block) + return precautions.

body.text: Full protocol: see the last-lipid-rescue module. In brief: STOP injecting · call for help ('possible LAST') · 100% O₂, secure airway (hypoxia accelerates toxicity) · seizures → benzodiazepine, avoid seizure-dose propofol · 20% lipid emulsion 1.5 mL/kg IBW bolus over 2-3 min, then 0.25 mL/kg/min (→ 0.5 if unstable), repeat bolus at 5 min, max ~12 mL/kg · arrest → CPR with REDUCED epi (10-100 mcg boluses), avoid vasopressin/CCB/β-blocker/propofol · prolonged resus (bupivacaine 60+ min), consider ECMO early · ICU ≥ 4-6 h (recurrence from redistribution). Bupivacaine is the most cardiotoxic ('fast in, slow out').
